Answer the questions.

1. What other things could you spill?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
spill something all over the floorknock over a bottle
You could spill coffee, soup, paint or cleaning liquid. I once knocked over a cup of coffee and spilt it all over my desk.
2. What might you forget to turn off?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
forget to turn off the cookercatch fireleave the tap on
You might forget to turn off the cooker, an iron or the lights. Forgetting the cooker can be dangerous because something could catch fire.
3. How else might a house flood?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
flood the apartmentleave the tap oncause a lot of damage
A washing machine could leak, a pipe could burst, or someone could leave the tap on. Any of these could flood the apartment.
4. How could you cause a lot of damage to a car?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
crash into the car in frontcause a lot of damage
You could crash into another car, hit a wall or reverse into something. Even a low-speed crash can cause a lot of damage.
5. What else can catch fire? How?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
catch fireforget to turn something offcause a lot of damage
Curtains, furniture or electrical equipment can catch fire. For example, an electrical fault can start a fire.
6. Where else might you slip? Why?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
slip and fall down the stairsspill something all over the floor
You might slip in a bathroom, on ice or on a wet supermarket floor because the surface is slippery.

4.2 You’re going to talk about an accident or a mistake.

First, listen to someone describing a big mistake and answer the questions.

Original MP3 embedded · 77.6s
A: I once fell asleep in an exam!

B: Oh, my word! How did you manage to do that?

A: Well, I was doing my final exams at university and for one of them I didn’t really revise until the day before, so I was studying all day and all night, you know, drinking loads of coffee all the time to keep me going.

B: You didn’t sleep at all?

A: A couple of hours in the evening – but, actually, I went for a quick run in the morning and had a cold shower and I basically thought I was OK. And then the first part of the exam went fine, too. They were mainly multiple-choice questions.

B: OK.

A: But then I came to some longer questions and I was struggling a bit and I just closed my eyes to concentrate …

B: Oh dear!

A: … and then the next thing I knew, a teacher was waking me up!

B: How long were you asleep?

A: It was the end of the exam!

B: Oh no! So, what happened? Did you fail?

A: Of course! I had to retake it. And luckily my average for the other exams was OK, so …

B: Just embarrassing.

A: Exactly! I felt a bit stupid!
After listening: read the script aloud and copy the speaker’s pace, sentence stress, rhythm, linking, pauses and intonation. Then shadow the recording almost simultaneously.
1. What was the mistake?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
fall asleep in an exammake a mistake
He fell asleep during an exam.
2. Why did it happen?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
revise for an examkeep me goingfall asleep in an exam
He had revised all day and all night, had slept very little and was exhausted.
3. How did he feel about it? What was the result of the mistake?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
retake an examfeel embarrassedmake a mistake
He felt embarrassed and a bit stupid. He failed the exam and had to retake it.
✎

Think of a time when you had an accident or made a mistake.

Answer the questions. Write down a maximum of ten words or phrases.

Try to answer about your own story before opening the sample answer. The sample is only a model of the language.
1. When did it happen?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
make a mistakehave an accident
It happened about two years ago when I was travelling with a friend.
2. What were you doing at the time?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
was / were + -ingturn up at the hotel
We were travelling to another city and I was checking our hotel booking on my phone.
3. Who were you with?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
with a friendwith my familyon my own
I was with a friend who had trusted me to organise the trip.
4. What caused the accident/mistake?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
mix up the datesmake a mistaketick the wrong box
I had mixed up the dates and booked the room for the following weekend.
5. What were the consequences?
ANSWER ORALLY FIRST
Recommended target collocations
what were the consequences?turn up at the hotelget charged extra
When we turned up at the hotel, there was no room for us, so we had to find another hotel and got charged much more.
USEFUL PHRASES

Keep the story going

How did you manage to do that?
Как тебе вообще удалось это сделать?
So what happened after that? Did you (lose your job)?
И что произошло после этого? Ты (потерял работу)?
And what happened in the end?
И чем всё закончилось?
How did you feel after all that?
Как ты себя чувствовал после всего этого?
